name: Xiaomi 17 Ultra

cameras.label: Leica 50MP 1-inch main camera (23mm)
cameras.notes: 50MP, 1" Light Fusion 1050L sensor with LOFIC HDR, f/1.67, 23mm equivalent and OIS are from Xiaomi's own spec pages (mi.com). Pixel pitch (1.6µm) and the Dual Pixel PDAF type are from GSMArena's spec table, not stated on the Xiaomi pages found. Binned pixel size and lens element count were not found and are left null. Xiaomi names the whole rear system 'VARIO-APO-SUMMILUX 1:1.67-2.9/14-100 ASPH.'. That is a name for the 14–100mm system, not a variable aperture on this camera. Newer models: the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max launched in China on 2026-09-23 (Notebookcheck, GSMArena). Neither is an Ultra model; GSMArena lists a 1/1.28" main sensor and a 1/1.56" 75mm periscope for the 18 Pro Max, both smaller than the 17 Ultra's 1" main and 1/1.4" telephoto sensors, so the Xiaomi 17 Ultra remains Xiaomi's top camera model and is the entry kept here.

cameras.label: Leica 50MP 14mm ultra-wide camera
cameras.notes: 50MP, Samsung JN5, 1/2.75", f/2.2, 14mm equivalent and 115° field of view are from Xiaomi's spec pages. Pixel pitch (0.64µm) is from GSMArena. Stabilisation is left null because the sources disagree: one summary of Xiaomi's page says OIS on all cameras, but GSMArena lists OIS only for the main and telephoto cameras. The AF type and the zoom factor Xiaomi shows in the camera app were not confirmed, so both are null.

cameras.label: Leica 200MP 75–100mm telephoto
cameras.notes: A continuous optical zoom telephoto: Xiaomi gives a 75–100mm equivalent range, reached by moving 3 lens groups, with the aperture going from f/2.39 at 75mm to f/2.96 at 100mm. eqFocalMm and aperture above are the 75mm end values. The 3.2x–4.3x optical-zoom range, the 0.56µm pixel pitch and PDAF are from GSMArena. Notebookcheck describes it as a sliding periscope module; the folded design is recorded with 'folded', and prism is null because no prism type was published. The 200MP 1/1.4" 'Samsung HPE' sensor is from Xiaomi's spec page. According to GSMArena, it records up to 4K 120fps and 8K 30fps like the main camera.

cameras.label: 50MP front camera
cameras.notes: 50MP is confirmed by Xiaomi. Sensor format (1/2.88") and pixel pitch (0.61µm) are from GSMArena. Aperture, equivalent focal length, AF type and stabilisation were not verified in the sources found and are left null.

computational.name: LOFIC HDR
computational.description: Sensor-level HDR technology on the 1-inch Light Fusion 1050L main sensor. Xiaomi credits it for high dynamic range and clean night photos.

summary: The Xiaomi 17 Ultra is Xiaomi's Leica co-engineered camera flagship. It pairs a 50MP 1-inch main camera (23mm, f/1.67) with a 50MP 14mm ultra-wide and a 200MP periscope telephoto with continuous optical zoom from 75 to 100mm. Notebookcheck's review singles out the overall package and the Leica APO zoom, and GSMArena reports 8K 30 fps recording on both the main and the telephoto camera. Xiaomi introduced it in December 2025 together with a Leica Edition that adds a mechanically rotating Control Ring around the round camera island. The Leica Edition's global version is the Leica Leitzphone powered by Xiaomi, introduced at MWC on 28 February 2026.

name: vivo X300 Ultra

cameras.label: 200MP ZEISS 35mm main camera (LYTIA 901)
cameras.notes: 200MP, LYTIA 901 sensor, 35mm focal length, OIS with a CIPA 6.5 stabilisation rating and AF are from vivo's own pages (vivo.com, shop.vivo.com). The 1/1.12" format and f/1.85 are from GSMArena's launch coverage, not found on vivo's pages. vivo does not state the AF type on the pages found, so the label is just 'AF'. Pixel pitch, binned pixel size and lens element count were not found and are left null. Unlike most phones, the main camera is a 35mm equivalent, not about 23–24mm. The 3D module arrangement (moduleLayout 'round-island') is only an approximation of the large circular camera island shown on vivo's pages.

cameras.label: 50MP ZEISS 14mm ultra-wide camera (LYT-818)
cameras.notes: 50MP, LYT-818 sensor, 14mm and the CIPA 6.0 stabilisation rating are from vivo's pages. The 1/1.28" format, f/2.0, 1.22µm pixel pitch, 116° field of view, Dual Pixel PDAF and OIS are from GSMArena's spec table. opticalZoom is null because no published factor relative to the 35mm main camera was found.

cameras.label: 200MP ZEISS 85mm Gimbal-Grade Telephoto (HP0)
cameras.notes: 200MP, 1/1.4" HP0 sensor, 85mm, 3° stabilisation with a CIPA 7.0 rating and the 'Gimbal-Grade Telephoto' name are from vivo's pages. GSMArena reports f/2.67 in its launch coverage (its spec table rounds this to f/2.7) and gives the 0.56µm pixel pitch, multi-directional PDAF and the periscope design. GSMArena lists '3.7x optical zoom', but that factor is not relative to the 35mm main camera, so opticalZoom is left null. The prism type was not published. vivo sells an optional telephoto extender: it gives a 400mm equivalent, and vivo says optional extenders reach up to 1600mm.

cameras.label: 50MP front camera
cameras.notes: Every value for this camera is from GSMArena's spec table (50MP, f/2.5, 24mm, 1/2.76", 0.64µm, AF), not from a vivo page. Stabilisation was not found and is left null.

computational.name: VS1+ Pro Imaging Chip
computational.description: A separate 6 nm imaging chip that processes RAW data before the main processor, handling noise, sharpness and dynamic range.

computational.name: Snapshot Engine
computational.description: A capture mode for fast action that uses 60 fps subject tracking and motion HDR processing, including on the telephoto camera.

summary: The vivo X300 Ultra is vivo's ZEISS co-branded camera flagship. It has three rear cameras at 14mm, 35mm and 85mm: a 50MP ultra-wide, a 200MP main camera with a 1/1.12-inch LYTIA 901 sensor, and a 200MP periscope telephoto with 3° gimbal-grade stabilisation. Instead of the usual 23–24mm main camera it uses a 35mm focal length, and it supports optional telephoto extenders, 10-bit Log video and 4K 120 fps Dolby Vision recording.

name: HUAWEI Pura 90 Pro Max / Pura 90s Pro Max

cameras.label: 50 MP Ultra Lighting HDR Camera
cameras.notes: 50 MP, the adjustable physical aperture (Huawei's spec page gives it as F1.4~F4.0) and OIS are from Huawei's global spec page for the Pura 90s Pro Max. 'aperture' is set to f/1.4, the widest end. apertureSteps is null because Huawei does not list the individual stops (reviews describe a 10-step aperture but do not list the f-numbers). The 1/1.28" format, the LOFIC sensor design and the RYYB colour filter are from GSMArena and Notebookcheck, not from Huawei's page. The 24mm equivalent focal length is from review coverage of the Pura 90s Pro Max (PetaPixel, Digital Camera World), not from Huawei. Pixel pitch, sensor model and AF type were not found and are left null. GSMArena reports that the global Pura 90s Pro Max (July 2026) uses the same camera hardware as the China-only Pura 90 Pro Max (April 2026), so this entry covers both. A Pura 90 Ultra appeared only in leaks and rumours in the searches made; no launch was found, so the Pura 90 Pro Max is treated as the top model of Huawei's 2026 Pura series. Reviews describe a rounded triangular camera island with the three lenses spread across the upper-left corner; moduleLayout 'triangle-square' is the closest of the available 3D arrangements, not an exact model of it.

cameras.label: 40 MP Ultra-Wide Angle Camera
cameras.notes: 40 MP and F2.2 are from Huawei's spec page. The 13mm equivalent and autofocus (with macro support) are from GSMArena. Sensor format, pixel pitch, stabilisation and the zoom factor were not found and are left null.

cameras.label: 200 MP Ultra Large Sensor Telephoto Camera
cameras.notes: 200 MP, F2.6 and OIS are from Huawei's spec page, and Huawei also advertises 20x telephoto video. The 1/1.28" format, the periscope design and 4x optical zoom are from GSMArena and Notebookcheck. GSMArena also reports a CIPA stabilisation rating of up to 7 stops, telemacro support and up to 20x 'lossless' zoom. The 89mm equivalent focal length and the RYYB colour filter on this sensor are from review coverage of the Pura 90s Pro Max (PetaPixel, Digital Camera World), not from Huawei. The opticalZoom value (4) is the figure published by GSMArena and Notebookcheck. Pixel pitch, AF type and prism type were not found and are left null.

cameras.label: 13 MP front camera
cameras.notes: 13 MP, f/2.0, the ultra-wide field of view and AF are from GSMArena's spec table, not from a Huawei page found. GSMArena also reports 4K 60fps video. Everything else was not found and is left null.

computational.name: XMAGE
computational.description: Huawei's name for its camera and image-processing system, advertised on this phone as the XMAGE AI Camera.

computational.name: True-to-Colour Camera 2.0
computational.description: An extra colour sensor in the camera module that Huawei uses to reproduce colours more accurately.

computational.name: AI Composition
computational.description: Shows on-screen icons and prompts that guide the user towards a better framing angle.

computational.name: Ultra Speed Snapshot
computational.description: A capture mode for photographing fast-moving subjects.

computational.name: Super Macro
computational.description: A close-up mode for photographing small subjects at short distances.

summary: The HUAWEI Pura 90 Pro Max is the top model of Huawei's 2026 Pura series. It launched in China in April 2026, and in July 2026 it went on sale globally as the Pura 90s Pro Max with the same camera hardware. It combines a 50 MP main camera with an adjustable physical aperture (F1.4 to F4.0), a 40 MP ultra-wide and a 200 MP periscope telephoto with 4x optical zoom that GSMArena reports uses a 1/1.28-inch sensor. The three rear cameras sit in Huawei's rounded triangular camera island.

name: OPPO Find X9 Ultra

cameras.label: Hasselblad 200MP Ultra-Sensing Main Camera
cameras.notes: 200MP, 1/1.12", f/1.5, 23mm, 84° field of view, a 7P lens (7 plastic elements), AF and 2-axis OIS are from OPPO's spec and product pages (oppo.com). The Sony LYTIA 901 sensor model and the 0.7µm pixel pitch (2.8µm binned) are from GSMArena's coverage, not from OPPO. OPPO does not name the AF type. OPPO also lists a 3.2MP f/2.4 camera (95° field of view, 3P lens) under 'Monochrome'; GSMArena calls it a true-colour camera. It has no role in this schema, so it is not listed as a camera. GSMArena reports a launch in China and globally on 21 April 2026. The newer Find X9s is a smaller model, not a camera flagship, so the Find X9 Ultra remains OPPO's top camera phone. The 3D module arrangement (moduleLayout 'round-island') is only an approximation of the large round 'Master Lens Design' camera module described on OPPO's pages.

cameras.label: 50MP Ultra Wide Camera
cameras.notes: 50MP, 14mm, 1/1.95", f/2.0, 123° field of view, a 6P lens and AF are from OPPO's pages. The 0.6x factor is the widest of the zoom steps OPPO lists (0.6x to 20x). The LYTIA 600 sensor model and the 0.8µm pixel pitch (1.6µm binned) are from GSMArena. OPPO's spec line for this camera does not mention OIS, so stabilisation is left null.

cameras.label: Hasselblad 200MP 3× Super Portrait Telephoto
cameras.notes: 200MP, 70mm, 1/1.28", f/2.2, 3x, 34° field of view, 2-axis OIS and a 15cm macro focus are from OPPO's pages. OPPO describes the optics as 'Prism(OIS)+3P+3P(AF)': a stabilised prism followed by two groups of 3 plastic elements, the second of which focuses. lensElements (6) is the total of those groups. The OV52A sensor model and the 0.61µm pixel pitch (2.45µm binned) are from GSMArena, not from OPPO. Its role is "telephoto" to tell it apart from the 10x camera, but it also uses folded (prism) optics.

cameras.label: Hasselblad 50MP 10× Ultra-Sensing Optical-Zoom Telephoto
cameras.notes: 50MP, 230mm, 1/2.75", f/3.5, 10x, 11° field of view, AF and 2-axis OIS are from OPPO's pages. OPPO describes the optics as '1G3P+PRISM': one glass and three plastic elements plus a prism, so lensElements is 4. GSMArena reports a quintuple-reflection prism, sensor-shift stabilisation and 20x 'optical-quality' zoom (460mm, the long end of the 14–460mm range OPPO advertises). The JNL sensor model and the 0.64µm pixel pitch (1.28µm binned) are from GSMArena.

cameras.label: 50MP front camera
cameras.notes: 50MP, f/2.4 and AF are from OPPO's spec page. The JN5 sensor model, the 1/2.75" format and the 0.64µm pixel pitch (1.28µm binned) are from GSMArena. The equivalent focal length, field of view and stabilisation were not found and are left null.

computational.name: LUMO Image Engine
computational.description: OPPO's set of computational photography algorithms for detail, dynamic range and colour, used across the zoom steps from 0.6x to 20x.

computational.name: Hasselblad Natural Colour Solution
computational.description: Colour processing tuned with Hasselblad that uses a multispectral sensor's white-balance measurements, for photos, motion photos and video.

computational.name: Hasselblad Master Mode
computational.description: A manual mode with ISO and shutter-speed control and 50MP JPEG MAX / RAW MAX output at six focal lengths from 14mm to 230mm.

computational.name: Hasselblad Portrait Mode
computational.description: A portrait mode for the 3x telephoto that renders background blur and uses the LUMO True Face algorithm for skin tones.

summary: The OPPO Find X9 Ultra is OPPO's Hasselblad-branded camera flagship, launched in April 2026. It has a 200MP 1/1.12-inch main camera (23mm, f/1.5), a 50MP 14mm ultra-wide and two periscope telephotos: a 200MP 3x camera at 70mm and a 50MP 10x camera at 230mm. OPPO covers a 14–460mm range and presents the 10x module as the first 50MP 10x optical telephoto.
